newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Pace of Hungary rate declines slows in Q2-c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Pace of Hungary rate declines slows in Q2-c.bank.

text.p: A two-year-long trend of falling interest rates in Hungary's corporate banking sector slowed in the second quarter of the year, the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) said in a statement on Friday.
"The trend of interest rate decline beginning in the autumn of 1995, has slowed down in the past few months," it said.

The average interest rate corporate loans of less than one year fell to 22 percent in June from 27.4 percent a year ago, but was down only 0.4 percentage points from the March level and was unchanged compared with May, the NBH said.
The average interest rate on deposits with a maturity of less than a year dropped to 17.6 percent in June from 20.5 a year ago, 18.2 percent in March and 17.9 percent in May.
The demand for corporate loans extended in forint increased substantially in June, the NBH added.

It said that the amount of loans of less than a year's duration extended in June rose by more than 30 percent from the May level to 33.7 billion forints. Loans with longer maturities jumped by almost 25 percent to 15.8 billion forints.
